questions.q: What does a VPN tunnel actually do?
options: Balances traffic across multiple servers
Creates an encrypted path across an untrusted network so the far side is reachable as if private
Translates domain names into IP addresses
Removes the need for firewall rules entirely
questions.explain: A VPN encrypts traffic across an untrusted network (usually the internet) so the remote network behaves as if it were local and private.

questions.q: What's the difference between a site-to-site VPN and a remote-access VPN?
options: Site-to-site connects two entire networks permanently; remote-access connects one device on demand
Remote-access is always faster than site-to-site
Site-to-site only works over UDP
There is no meaningful difference
questions.explain: Site-to-site VPNs permanently link two networks, while remote-access VPNs connect an individual device to a network as needed.

options: A load balancer for administrative traffic
A single, hardened server that is the only allowed entry point for administrative access into a private subnet
A DNS server dedicated to internal lookups
A backup NAT gateway
questions.explain: A bastion host is a deliberately hardened chokepoint — the only machine permitted to initiate SSH or RDP connections into a private subnet.

questions.q: After connecting to a VPN, why might an engineer still need to go through a bastion host to reach a database server?
options: VPNs don't support database connections
The database's security group still only allows inbound traffic from the bastion host specifically
Bastion hosts replace the need for a VPN
Database servers never accept SSH connections
questions.explain: Each security layer narrows the next: the database's own rules may still require traffic to originate from the bastion host, even for someone already on the VPN.

questions.q: Do VPNs and bastion hosts replace firewall and security-group rules?
options: Yes, they make firewall rules unnecessary
No, they add additional layers on top of those existing rules
Only for inbound traffic, not outbound
Only in cloud environments, not on-premises
questions.explain: VPNs and bastion hosts narrow who can attempt a connection, but the underlying firewall and security-group rules still apply as additional layers.
